newsitem.title: UK: Britons object to violence in ads after massacre.
newsitem.headline: Britons object to violence in ads after massacre.

text.p: Britain's television regulatory body said on Tuesday viewer complaints about violence in advertisements had risen since a gunman shot dead 16 children and their teacher at a Scottish primary school in March.
The Independent Television Commission (ITC) said in its latest monthly report viewers had complained that two ads in particular were either violent or reminded them of violence.
One was for Skittles, a type of candy, that showed brightly dressed gangsters with stylised fruit heads "shooting" cartoon fruits at a group of children.
Some viewers said the ad reminded them of the massacre in the Scottish town of Dunblane.
The ITC said it decided not to uphold the complaints, but had advised caution over showing weapons in advertisements.

"Although the ITC decided not to uphold the complaints, it did advise the television companies to take account of the continuing strength of feeling over the depiction of weaponry...," the ITC said in its report on complaints received in August.
An ITC spokeswoman told Reuters: "There is a greater sensitivity...You do not want to (do anything) that would bring back distressing memories."
The commission said it also decided not to uphold complaints about a different ad for Metz, a schnapps drink, that showed a male presenter wearing a ski mask.
Viewers said the image was disturbing because the man reminded them of a terrorist or rapist, but the ITC said that was not the intent of the advertiser.
The ITC also received complaints about ads viewers said were too sexually explicit.
It received 72 complaints about an ad for a headache remedy, Hedex Ibuprofen, that featured a couple who had sex after the woman's headache was cured.
Some complainants said the commercial was "soft porn" and the imagery was too explicit for children who might be watching.
The ITC upheld the complaints, saying the sexual innuendo made the ad unsuitable for broadcast before 9pm. The campaign created by Ogilvy & Mather advertising agency has now ended.
The ITC also dealt with 27 complaints about the People newspaper's advertisement for what it described as its "hottest ever sex guide for lovers who just can't wait".
This included shots of a partially undressed couple kissing on the stairs.
A number of viewers said the ad was "pornographic" and two objected to the ad being shown during a television programme about rape.
ITC did not upheld the complaints, but advised television companies to avoid scheduling advertisements with sexual content during programmes that dealt with sexual violence.
